title: Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, IBS and pancreatitis
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's digestive condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for ulcerative colitis.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his ulcerative colitis. He reports that his symptoms have been well-controlled over the last several months. He denies any acute abdominal pain, fever, or changes in bowel habits. He states that his energy levels are stable and he is able to perform his daily activities without significant discomfort. He currently takes mesalamine and reports consistent adherence to the prescribed regimen. He notes that his gastrointestinal symptoms remain quiescent at this time.

Medication List
- Mesalamine 2.5g daily
- Amlodipine 5mg daily
- Lisinopril 10mg daily

Review of Systems
The patient reports no recent fevers, chills, or night sweats. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. He reports no recent joint pain or muscle weakness. He denies any recent weight loss or changes in appetite.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his spouse. He retired five years ago and enjoys gardening and walking. He denies tobacco use and reports minimal social alcohol consumption.

Family History
Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No family history of inflammatory bowel disease is reported.

Exam
The patient is an alert and oriented 86-year-old male in no acute distress. He appears healthy and well-nourished. Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender to palpation. Bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants. No masses are palpable.

Assessment
The patient is an 86-year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis. He is currently in remission and remains stable on his current dose of mesalamine.

Plan
1. Continue current medication regimen as prescribed.
2. Maintain current dose of mesalamine for ulcerative colitis management.
3. Follow up in 6 months for a routine evaluation.
